subject: MAP: POC provisioning sprint — API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering
messages:
From: Alice Jensen <alice@acmehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff - provisioning needs for POC environment

Thanks Stephanie and Marissa — excited to get started. Per our internal evaluation plan, we need a POC environment that mirrors our production network for a two-week assessment:

- Short list of requirements:
  * API keys scoped to project: short-lived keys + rotation guide
  * Org setup: role mappings for engineers and security reviewers
  * IP allowlist: our egress CIDR(s) and test runner IPs
  * VPC peering: one-way peering from our VPC to Redwood's managed VPC (or equivalent peering arrangement)

Can you please confirm:
1) What information you need from our side to provision the org and generate keys?
2) Typical lead times for peering requests and any template we should use?
3) Any additional constraints for SOC2/home region (we are in us-west2)?

Attached: Acme_Eval_Scope.pdf (high-level requirements).

Goal: complete environment provision and first smoke tests within 5 business days of kickoff.

Thanks,
Alice Jensen
Director, Platform Engineering
AcmeHealth

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jensen <alice@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff - provisioning needs for POC environment

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. We can meet the 5-business-day target with a tight sprint and one short kickoff call. High-level plan from our side:

Sprint 1 (Day 0-2): intake + org + initial keys\- We will create a RW project/org for Acme with three role buckets: admin (security), engineer (dev/test), observer (audit).\- We issue one project-scoped API key (time-limited) for the test harness and provide instructions to rotate.\- Deliverable: redwood_poc_checklist.xlsx (provisioning tasks + owner) — attached.

Sprint 2 (Day 2-4): network allowlist + peering\- We need your peering CIDR(s) and the NetOps contact to submit the peering. Typical peering window is 24-48 hours once both sides accept, but allow 72 hours for DNS propagation and routing ACL checks.\- If you cannot peer, we can provide a tightly-scoped static egress IP instead for the POC.

Sprint 3 (Day 4-5): validation + smoke tests\- We'll run tokenized smoke tests and share latency/cost dashboards.

Immediate asks for you:
- Confirm NetOps contact and CIDR(s) for allowlist + peering\- Confirm which engineers need admin vs engineer roles (emails)

I suggest a 30-min kickoff at 11:00 PT today to align. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Tel: +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jensen <alice@acmehealth.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff - provisioning needs for POC environment

Thanks — adding a few technical clarifications from the infra side so the MAP items are actionable. Quoting Stephanie above for context:

> We will create a RW project/org for Acme with three role buckets...

What we will provision and what we need from you:
- Org + RBAC: we will create a top-level Acme org and (optionally) a staging sub-org. Please provide user emails for:
  * admin: 1-2 security contacts
  * engineer: up to 6 engineers for the POC
  * observer: one audit contact
- API key model:
  * We will generate a project-scoped API key valid for 30 days. For best practice, we recommend integrating with your secret manager and rotate daily for automated runs.
  * If you require HSM-backed keys, we can exchange a KMS integration checklist; otherwise standard keys are fine for evaluation.
- IP allowlist / peering notes:
  * Provide 2-3 CIDR ranges you can commit for the 2-week window. Example: 34.200.16.0/24
  * For VPC peering we need: VPC ID, account/project ID, region, and a NetOps contact who can accept the peering on your side.
  * If ephemeral CI runners are used, include those public egress IPs; otherwise we will test from our static egress.
- Firewall & routes:
  * If you use strict egress filtering, add redwood-ingress.example.com and our peering CIDRs to allow DNS and TLS handshakes.

I'll prepare a peering template (VPC peering request) and drop it in the MAP record after the kickoff.

Marissa
Senior Cloud Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
